## Landed and closed

**Gerrit change 1974 — MERGED** (302 insertions, 0 deletions, 0 unresolved comments).
`LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on patch set 2; Gerrit rebased server-side to PS3 and
submitted. CI green across the full matrix — lint + type-check, pytest on ubuntu py3.11/3.12/
3.13 and macos py3.13, the bounded mutation gate, identity, packaging/optionality, artifact
provenance, and pip-audit.

Closed `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135`. Verified afterwards that the
ticket carries exactly ONE `caused_by` edge, so the known duplicate-edge defect did not bite
(`10d0`'s idempotent caused_by write landed on main shortly before this change).

**Patch set 2 exists because of the review.** `LLM-Review` passed PS1 with one advisory
finding: the `except OSError: return os.sep` branch of `detached_child_cwd` was documented
as load-bearing to the never-raise contract but had no test. That was a real gap in my own
oracle — a documented invariant with no test is precisely what rots — so I added
`test_durable_cwd_never_raises_when_the_callers_own_directory_is_gone`, which reaches that
branch the only way it can be reached (a RELATIVE tracker resolved from an already-dead cwd,
sending `realpath` through `getcwd()`). Removing the guard fails that test and only that
test, so the sixth mutant is killed as precisely as the first five.

### AC disposition, stated plainly

- AC 1 (a drain child from a since-removed worktree resolves and drains) — **met**, proven by
  the before/after replication on this store and by the held-out unit test.
- AC 2 — **met via its own "or an equivalent reproduction does" clause**, not by the three
  named entries. Those three are blocked by a second, independent defect
  (`spongy-illjudged-terrier`, 569c-931f-69a2-4c1d): their enrichment prompt exceeds the model
  context window, so they cycle forever. Ticking this box on the equivalent-reproduction clause
  rather than silently implying the named entries drained.
- AC 3 (lint, typecheck, CI pytest green) — **met**.

Anyone tracking `958e`'s "the WARNING no longer fires on an ordinary write": it still fires
on this store (observed at 429.6 ms and 648.5 ms during this session), and it will keep firing
until 569c lands too. That is the honest end state of this ticket, not a regression in it.
